title: Adaptive export formats and CDC checkpointing for tenant-friendly scheduled usage dumps
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Large customers generate extremely high-cardinality, high-volume usage streams. Our current scheduled CSV dumps hit two simultaneous pain points: (1) CSV blowup and slow downstream processing for high-cardinality events, and (2) inefficient incremental exports causing repeated full-file re-exports and large egress costs. We also lack a stable checkpointing mechanism for tenant-level incremental exports when source tables are compacted or archived.

Proposed solution: Implement an adaptive export pipeline that produces tenant-targeted scheduled exports in either compressed CSV or Parquet based on per-tenant heuristics, plus a CDC-based incremental layer using stable checkpoints (stream offsets + snapshot UUIDs). Key features: (a) format selection policy (CSV for small tenants or legacy customers, Parquet for high-cardinality / enterprise tenants), (b) per-tenant column normalization and schema evolution metadata injected into the manifest, (c) CDC checkpointing that persists offset + source snapshot id in a durable offsets table (tenant-scoped), (d) idempotent export manifests (UUID + hash) and resumable S3 multipart upload support, and (e) rate-limited export workers that respect tenant export quotas and backpressure signals.

Why different from existing work: Unlike our previous resumable download and manifest efforts, this ticket focuses on intelligent format selection and a first-class CDC checkpoint model to minimize repeated reprocessing and to enable consistent incremental deltas even when upstream compaction occurs. It also adds an explicit per-tenant quota/enforcement layer to avoid noisy-neighbor export storms.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled export jobs can produce either CSV or Parquet files based on tenant policy and record count thresholds
CDC-based incremental runs produce delta files using persisted checkpoint offsets; repeated runs are idempotent and do not re-export already-committed events
Export manifest contains a stable schema section including column canonicalization map and schema version
S3 multipart uploads are resumable after worker restarts and manifest UUID + hash are used for dedup detection in downstream consumers
Per-tenant export throughput is limited by configured quotas; quota violations are logged and surfaced to console and billing dashboards
Regression: existing small-tenant CSV exports and webhook deliveries continue to function without behavior change unless tenant opts into Parquet
technical_notes: Format selection heuristic: if estimated file size > 80MB OR unique column cardinality > 2000 -> select Parquet + Snappy; else CSV + gzip
CDC checkpoint schema: {tenant_id, source_stream, offset, snapshot_uuid, last_emitted_ts, manifest_uuid} stored in postgres offsets table sharded by tenant_id range
Implementation plan: streaming extraction uses existing materialized usage view; Delta generator computes tombstones and new rows by comparing last checkpoint offset to current WAL position
Backpressure: export workers support soft-rate (tokens per second) and burst budgets; workers will return 429-like status in webhook mode and schedule exponential backoff for retries

Manifest design: top-level manifest.json per export run with fields: tenant_id, run_id, format, schema_version, canonical_columns[], file_parts[], checksum; downstream consumers should be able to consume manifest first and then fetch parts in parallel
S3 uploads: use aws-sdk multipart upload with part size 50MB default, persist upload id in offsets table for resumability
Security: all exported artifacts use customer KMS key when tenant has KMS enabled; temporary presigned URLs expire in 24 hours by default

Observability: emit per-export metrics (export_size_bytes, duration_ms, rows_exported, format_selected, checkpoint_lag_ms, upload_retries) to metrics ingestion (datadog) and correlate with billing pipeline
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable Parquet exports for two opt-in enterprise tenants and run scheduled exports side-by-side with current CSV dumps for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (quota enforcement): deploy tenant-level export throttling flags behind feature flag; turn on hard limits for a subset of noisy tenants
Phase 3 (CDC migration): run CDC-based incremental exports for canary tenants; maintain fallback full-export path if checkpoint missing
Phase 4 (general availability): flip policy to auto-select formats for tenants above cardinality threshold; update docs and billing descriptions
Rollback: keep previous full-CSV flush path available and a console toggle to force legacy mode per-tenant
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: persistent checkpoint_staleness (checkpoint_lag_ms > 24h) for any tenant -> P1
SLO: 95% of scheduled exports must complete within SLA window (6h) for enterprise tier
Dashboards: per-tenant export throughput, export_size_histogram, upload_retry_count, manifest_validation_failures
Logging: include manifest_uuid and tenant_id in all export logs; correlate with billing export traces
test_plan: Unit tests for format selection heuristic covering edge cases (boundary cardinality and size estimates)
Integration test that simulates WAL advancement and validates CDC checkpointing keeps deltas idempotent across restarts
Chaos test: kill worker mid-upload and ensure multipart resumability and manifest dedup detection works
E2E test in staging: run scheduled exports for 10 synthetic tenants with varying cardinality and verify downstream parquet and csv consumers process without schema errors
Security test: validate KMS-encrypted exports can be decrypted by authorized accounts only
